newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE GAS OIL DOWN BUT BRENT DIP CORRECTIVE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE GAS OIL DOWN BUT BRENT DIP CORRECTIVE.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Gas oil's recent rally looks likely to have run out of steam after it closed below trendline support, but it's downside potential is also increased by bearish momentum indicators.
* The outlook for Brent remains positive after piercing $19 this week. The downside is seen as "just a correction" and it is expected to find support $18.40, before moving up again.

IPE Brent crude futures are likely to hold slightly weaker after closing below support on Thursday, but analysts saw the market well supported at the lower levels and possibly keeping the longer term uptrend intact.

However, they said gas oil's recent rally seemed to have run out of steam after it too closed below trendline support, but its downside potential is also increased by bearish momentum indicators. Tom James analyst at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore said, "Gas oil looks likely to be the only market with any real downside potential with Brent and NYMEX crude and products staring to look a bit over sold."

He said Tuesday's exhaustive gap up (from Monday's $173.50 high and Tuesday's $175 low ) has now been fill by the combination of Wednesday's key top reversal and yesterday's price action that saw it close below trendline support.

He expected the next downside target to be the $170.75 level a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the recent rally, but then psychological, trendline and moving average support comes into play at around $170.
Wee Woon Whai, analyst at MMS International in Singapore said, "The outlook remains positive after Brent broke through $19 this week."
"The current downside is just a correction and I expect prices will stay weak for Friday and Monday but the market will find support around $18.40."
"If it can hold and consolidate above this level then the uptrend remains intact and there is still plenty of room for it to go higher again," she added.
James said, "Brent's close below uptrend support that has been in place since July 15 was bearish, but the divergence of the moving average lines and neutral RSI's could become supportive".
Some analysts said the Brent market was looking overbought and due for a correction but thought that the $19.60 barrier would be cleared eventually, setting the market to trade just below $20.
